# Diallels over environments and the biplot

## 1 Abstract

A diallel grown in several environments shows whether combining ability
is stable.
[`GriffingEnv()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/GriffingEnv.md)
pools Griffing’s analyses over environments and splits each line into
its main effect and its interaction with environments. The biplot of the
cross means shows the best general combiners and the best crosses on one
graph.

## 2 A diallel over several environments

[`GriffingEnv()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/GriffingEnv.md)
pools Griffing’s analyses of the same diallel in several environments.
Each line of the analysis is a projection of the table of cross means,
so the sum over environments of a line’s sum of squares splits into the
line itself and its interaction with environments. The example simulates
six parents of Method 2 in three environments with gca \\\times\\
environment effects:

``` r

d <-
  DiallelSim(
      Parents = 6
    , Method  = 2
    , Rep     = 3
    , Env     = 3
    , Mean    = 50
    , gca     = 4
    , sca     = 2
    , rec     = 0
    , gcaEnv  = 1.5
    , scaEnv  = 1
    , EnvSD   = 2
    , Block   = 1
    , Error   = 3
    , seed    = 1
    )
fe <-
  GriffingEnv(
      y      = y
    , Rep    = Rep
    , Cross1 = Cross1
    , Cross2 = Cross2
    , Env    = Env
    , data   = d
    , Method = 2
    , Model  = 2
    )
fe$ANOVA
```

              Df  Sum Sq Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)
    Env        2   81.91   40.95  9.1418  0.015084 *
    Rep(Env)   6   26.88    4.48  1.5694  0.161861
    gca        5 2073.78  414.76 48.4875 1.088e-06 ***
    sca       15  200.96   13.40  5.1141 7.288e-05 ***
    gca:Env   10   85.54    8.55  2.9968  0.002076 **
    sca:Env   30   78.59    2.62  0.9178  0.593124
    Error    120  342.52    2.85
    ---
    Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

``` r

fe$Genetic.Components
```

            Components
    gca     16.4760483
    sca      3.5924821
    gca:Env  0.7417799
    sca:Env -0.2347162
    Error    2.8543549
    gca/sca  4.5862576

In Model 2 gca and sca are tested against their interactions with
environments. The gca effects in each environment show which parents
combine well everywhere:

``` r

plot(x = fe, which = c("gca", "gcaenv", "sca", "residuals", "qq")[2])
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## 3 A biplot of the crosses

`plot(fit, which = "biplot")` draws the table of cross means as a biplot
(Yan and Hunt 2002): the table of a cross and its reciprocal averaged,
the selfs left out and filled by a rank-two fit, centred on the tester
(column) means, and its first two principal components with the singular
values split between parents and testers. Parents far along the
average-tester axis (dashed) combine well in general; a parent close to
a tester’s vector combines well with that tester.

``` r

g4 <-
  Griffing(
      y          = Yield
    , Rep        = Rep
    , Cross1     = Cross1
    , Cross2     = Cross2
    , data       = GriffingData4
    , Method     = 4
    , Model      = 1
    , Reciprocal = c("combined", "split")[1]
    )
plot(x = g4, which = c("gca", "sca", "biplot", "residuals", "qq")[3])
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

When specific combining ability is large the two axes show mainly the
sca pattern; the parent with the largest gca effect is printed in bold.

## 4 Summary

The gca \\\times\\ environment and sca \\\times\\ environment lines show
whether combining ability holds across environments; the biplot shows
which parents and crosses stand out.

## 5 References

Griffing, B. (1956). Concept of general and specific combining ability
in relation to diallel crossing systems. *Australian Journal of
Biological Sciences*, 9(4), 463–493.

Quantitative Genetic Analysis*. Kalyani Publishers, New Delhi.

Yan, W. and Hunt, L. A. (2002). Biplot analysis of diallel data. *Crop
Science*, 42(1), 21–30.

Zhang, Y. and Kang, M. S. (1997). DIALLEL-SAS: a SAS program for
Griffing’s diallel analyses. *Agronomy Journal*, 89(2), 176–182.
